newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to offer 220 mln shares in Securities Group.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to offer 220 mln shares in Securities Group.

text.p: Kuwait will offer 220 million shares in Securities Group for public subscription in the second stage of a privatisation bid, the sale manager said on Tuesday.
National Bank of Kuwait (NBK), the underwriter and manager and of the sale by the Kuwait Investment Authority(KIA), said the subscription price was set at 215 fils per share.

KIA, the state investment arm, earlier this month sold 80 million shares in the brokerage and investment firm by public auction to private investors for 22.4 million dinars. The auction closed at 280 fils from a starting price of 136 fils.
There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
The minimum subscription is for 5,000 shares and the maximum is for five million shares, NBK said in a statement. The offer opens on November 3 and closes on November 20.
Only nationals of the Gulf Arab states -- Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar -- can buy shares of Kuwaiti firms.
Officials said the sale was part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications.
Securities Group is not listed on the Kuwait Stock Exchange.
The privatisation plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is supervised by KIA.
